statement: Learner multiplies the degree of financial leverage by (1 - tax rate), treating DFL as a post-tax quantity. Tax scales EPS and EBT by the same factor, so it cancels out of a ratio of percentage changes and never enters DFL.
signature: selects an option equal to the correct DFL multiplied by (1 - t)
error magnitude tracks the tax rate supplied in the stem
canned_hint_l1: Hold the tax rate fixed and move EBIT by 10%. Does the percentage change in EPS depend on that rate at all?
canned_hint_l2: Tax multiplies both EPS and EBT by the same factor. What happens to a constant that appears in both halves of a ratio?

statement: Learner computes Contribution / EBIT when asked for financial leverage, or EBIT / EBT when asked for operating leverage. The two degrees are confused because both are ratios built from EBIT.
signature: selects the value of the other leverage measure
canned_hint_l1: Which risk is this measuring - the cost structure above EBIT, or the financing below it?
canned_hint_l2: Operating leverage looks upward to contribution and fixed costs. Financial leverage looks downward to interest.

statement: Learner subtracts interest from the numerator as well as the denominator, computing (EBIT - Interest) / (EBIT - Interest) style expressions, or nets interest out of EBIT before forming the ratio.
signature: selects a value at or near 1.00 regardless of the figures given
canned_hint_l1: What does the numerator represent before any interest is paid?
canned_hint_l2: EBIT is the top line of this ratio, untouched. Interest is subtracted only once, in the denominator.
